description: Comprehensive accepted five-letter English vocabulary for EmniFun Game 1.
sourceStrategy: Moby Words II single_5az.txt provides the broad five-letter single-word base.
Moby Words II crosswd.txt and crswd-d.txt provide supplementary established word-game vocabulary, including legitimate inflected forms.
Wordnik wordlist provides an independent supplementary English lexical source.
Moby names, places, and acronym/abbreviation side lists are used to remove source-flagged non-standard entries when they are not supported by the Moby single-word base.
Moby common.txt is used only as corroboration when filtering obvious malformed or short-form-like Moby entries.

sources.name: Moby Words II
sources.license: Original Moby Words II content was released to the public domain; mirror modifications are dedicated to CC0 1.0.
sources.role: Broad lexical base, crossword vocabulary, and source classification side lists.

sources.name: Wordnik Wordlist
sources.role: Independent supplementary English wordlist for games and word-based applications.

filtering: Keep exactly five ASCII alphabetic letters A-Z.
Exclude source-flagged proper names, places, acronyms, and abbreviations when they lack Moby single-word support.
Exclude only unmistakable malformed or short-form-like Moby entries when they also lack independent lexical corroboration.
Preserve uncommon, archaic, variant, and legitimate inflected English words supported by the selected sources.
Do not impose any numerical vocabulary cap or target size.
The final size is determined by source coverage and the filtering rules.
pipelineNote: Generated automatically by scripts/generate-game1-vocabulary.mjs. The complete vocabulary is generated from the selected lexical sources; it is not manually typed and is never truncated to a fixed count.
answersSeparation: valid-guesses.json is the comprehensive accepted-guess vocabulary; answers.json is a separately curated daily-answer subset.
wordCountNote: There is intentionally no maximum such as 10,000, 15,000, or 20,000 words.
